_meta.note: Each rule maps to one WCAG 2.1 success criterion. wcag_sc is the dotted SC number; wcag is the rubric key. fix_mode: auto = deterministic engine fix; ai-assisted = engine drafts, human approves; human-only = must be verified by a person.

docx.title: Image missing alt text
docx.description: Every non-decorative image must carry a description in its <wp:docPr descr> attribute. Screen readers announce this text in place of the image.

docx.title: Document title not set
docx.description: The core properties <dc:title> element must be non-empty. Assistive technology announces the title when the document is opened.

docx.title: Document language not declared
docx.description: The <w:lang> element in settings.xml must declare a BCP 47 language code (e.g. 'en-US'). Screen readers use this to select the correct pronunciation engine.

docx.title: Table has no header row
docx.description: Every data table must mark its first row as a header row (<w:tblHeader>) so assistive technology can announce column labels when navigating cells.

docx.title: Insufficient colour contrast
docx.description: Text colour against its background must meet the 4.5:1 minimum contrast ratio for normal-sized text (3:1 for large text ≥18pt or 14pt bold).

docx.title: Heading structure incorrect
docx.description: Heading styles must not skip levels (e.g. Heading 1 → Heading 3 with no Heading 2). Skipped levels break navigation for screen reader users who jump by heading.

docx.title: Link text not descriptive
docx.description: Hyperlink display text must describe the destination. Generic phrases such as 'click here', 'read more', or bare URLs are not descriptive out of context.

docx.title: Language of parts not set
docx.description: Runs of text in a different language from the document default must declare their language via <w:lang>. Without this, screen readers mispronounce foreign words.

docx.title: Long document has no bookmarks
docx.description: Documents longer than 10 pages should contain named bookmarks so users can jump to key sections without reading linearly.

docx.title: Floating text may disrupt reading order
docx.description: Text boxes and other floating shapes have an undefined position in the document's reading order. Screen readers may announce them out of sequence relative to surrounding paragraph text.

docx.title: Instructions rely on sensory characteristics
docx.description: Instructions that identify content solely by shape, visual position, size, or sound cannot be understood by users who are blind or deaf. Re-word to include a non-sensory alternative.

docx.title: Information conveyed by colour alone
docx.description: Hyperlinks with underlines removed rely on colour as the sole visual cue. Users who cannot distinguish colours will miss the link indicator. Restore the underline or add another non-colour cue.

docx.title: Text baked into an image
docx.description: An image appears to contain readable text. Text rendered into images cannot be resized, translated, or read by assistive technology. Replace with real document text.

docx.title: Non-text element has insufficient contrast
docx.description: A shape border or drawing element has a contrast ratio below 3:1 against its adjacent background. Informational graphics and UI components must meet this threshold so they remain visible to low-vision users.

docx.title: Embedded control may trap keyboard focus
docx.description: The document contains an interactive control (form field, ActiveX object, or embedded object) that may not allow keyboard focus to leave. Verify the user can move away using Tab or Escape.

docx.title: Heading or label is not descriptive
docx.description: Every heading must clearly describe the topic of its section. Vague or empty headings (e.g. 'Section 1', 'Untitled') prevent screen reader users from understanding the document's structure at a glance.

docx.title: Content control has no accessible name
docx.description: A structured document tag (content control) does not carry an accessible name in its w:alias or w:tag attribute. Assistive technology announces this name when focus reaches the control.

pptx.title: Image missing alt text
pptx.description: Every non-decorative image must have a non-empty description in the picture alternative text field. Screen readers announce this when moving through slides.

pptx.title: Slide title not set
pptx.description: Each slide must have a Title placeholder with non-empty text. Assistive technology reads the slide title when the user moves between slides.

pptx.title: Slide title duplicates another slide
pptx.description: Each slide's title should be unique across the deck. Duplicate titles make it impossible to distinguish slides by title alone when navigating by ear.

pptx.title: Document language not declared
pptx.description: The presentation must declare a default BCP 47 language code in its core document properties.

pptx.title: Reading order undefined
pptx.description: The tab order of shapes on each slide must match the intended visual reading order. Undefined or reversed order causes screen readers to announce content out of sequence.

pptx.title: Table has no header row
pptx.description: Every table must have a header row defined in the table style so assistive technology can announce column labels when navigating cells.

pptx.title: Insufficient colour contrast
pptx.description: Text colour against the slide background must meet the 4.5:1 minimum contrast ratio for normal-sized text.

pptx.title: Link text not descriptive
pptx.description: Hyperlink display text must describe the destination. Generic phrases such as 'click here' or bare URLs are not descriptive out of context.

pptx.title: Animation interferes with reading
pptx.description: Slide animations must not hide or reorder content during playback in a way that prevents assistive technology from reading the slide correctly.

pptx.title: Instructions rely on sensory characteristics
pptx.description: Instructions that identify content solely by shape, visual position, size, or sound cannot be understood by users who are blind or deaf. Re-word to include a non-sensory alternative.

pptx.title: Text box clips content at 200% zoom
pptx.description: A text box with fixed dimensions may clip its content when text is enlarged to 200%. Users who need large text should be able to read all slide content without horizontal scrolling or loss of content.

pptx.title: Text baked into an image
pptx.description: An image appears to contain readable text. Text rendered into images cannot be resized, translated, or read by assistive technology. Replace with real slide text.

pptx.title: Wide table may not reflow at narrow viewport
pptx.description: A table wider than the slide content area may require two-dimensional scrolling when the presentation is viewed at 320 CSS pixels. Prefer narrower tables or portrait layouts that reflow to one column.

pptx.title: Non-text element has insufficient contrast
pptx.description: A shape border or informational graphic has a contrast ratio below 3:1 against its background. UI components and graphics that convey meaning must meet this threshold for low-vision users.

pptx.title: Fixed line spacing may clip text
pptx.description: Text runs with an exact (fixed) line height setting may clip descenders or clip adjacent lines when a user's OS increases text spacing. Prefer proportional line spacing over an exact point value.

pptx.title: Embedded control may trap keyboard focus
pptx.description: The presentation contains an embedded control (ActiveX, OLE object) that may not allow keyboard focus to move away. Verify the user can leave the control using Tab or Escape.

pptx.title: Placeholder focus order may not match reading order
pptx.description: The tab order of placeholders on a slide is determined by their z-index, which may not match the intended visual reading sequence. Reorder placeholders so keyboard navigation follows reading order.

pptx.title: Slide title placeholder is empty
pptx.description: A slide has a Title placeholder that exists but contains no text. An empty title provides no navigation landmark for screen reader users jumping between slides by heading.

pptx.title: Language of parts not marked
pptx.description: Text runs in a language different from the presentation's default must declare their language via the a:rPr lang attribute. Without this, screen readers mispronounce foreign-language passages.

pptx.title: Embedded control has no accessible name
pptx.description: An ActiveX or OLE control embedded in the presentation does not expose an accessible name or role. Assistive technology cannot identify or operate a control whose name and role are not declared.

xlsx.title: Image missing alt text
xlsx.description: Embedded images must have alternative text in the picture properties. Screen readers announce this when focus reaches the image.

xlsx.title: Document title not set
xlsx.description: The workbook's core properties <dc:title> element must be non-empty. Assistive technology announces the title when the file is opened.

xlsx.title: Document language not declared
xlsx.description: The workbook must declare a language in its styles.xml. Without this, screen readers cannot select the correct pronunciation engine.

xlsx.title: Data range has no header row
xlsx.description: Every ListObject (formal table) must have a header row. Without headers, assistive technology cannot identify what each column represents.

xlsx.title: Generic table name
xlsx.description: A formal table's DisplayName must not use Excel's auto-generated default (Table1, Table2, etc.). A descriptive name helps assistive technology and formula users identify the table's purpose.

xlsx.title: Sheet name duplicates another sheet
xlsx.description: Worksheet tab names should be unique across the workbook, even when they're not Excel's generic defaults. Duplicate names make it impossible to distinguish sheets by name alone.

xlsx.title: Generic sheet name
xlsx.description: Worksheet tab names must not use Excel's defaults (Sheet1, Sheet2, etc.). Meaningful names let screen reader users understand what each sheet contains before navigating to it.

xlsx.title: Merged cells break navigation
xlsx.description: Merged cells break keyboard navigation for screen reader users. Use unmerged cells with visual centering as a substitute.

xlsx.title: Hidden content
xlsx.description: Hidden rows, columns, or sheets may contain information that assistive technology cannot reach, creating a gap between what the visual user sees and what is accessible.

xlsx.title: Blank worksheet
xlsx.description: A visible sheet with no cell data, charts, or images is an empty stop for screen reader users tabbing through the workbook. Delete it or add content.

xlsx.title: Link text not descriptive
xlsx.description: A cell hyperlink's display text is empty, generic ('click here'), or the raw URL. Covers both standard cell hyperlinks and =HYPERLINK() formula cells, which never appear in the worksheet's own hyperlinks list.

xlsx.title: Instructions rely on sensory characteristics
xlsx.description: Instructions that identify content solely by shape, visual position, size, or sound cannot be understood by users who are blind or deaf. Re-word to include a non-sensory alternative.

xlsx.title: Information conveyed by colour alone
xlsx.description: A conditional-format colour scale or colour-coded status indicator conveys meaning through colour alone. Users who cannot distinguish colours will miss this information. Add a text label, icon, or pattern to supplement the colour cue.

xlsx.title: Insufficient colour contrast
xlsx.description: Cell text colour against its background must meet the 4.5:1 minimum contrast ratio for normal-sized text (3:1 for large text ≥18pt or 14pt bold).

xlsx.title: Text baked into an image
xlsx.description: An embedded image appears to contain readable text. Text rendered into images cannot be resized, translated, or read by assistive technology. Replace with real cell content.

xlsx.title: Non-text element has insufficient contrast
xlsx.description: A drawing shape border or fill has a contrast ratio below 3:1 against its background. Informational graphics and UI components must meet this threshold so they remain visible to low-vision users.

xlsx.title: Language of parts cannot be declared
xlsx.description: SpreadsheetML rich-text run properties (CT_RPrElt) have no language element, so language-of-parts cannot be recorded in the file. Text in a language different from the workbook default cannot be marked up and must be re-authored to avoid mispronunciation.

xlsx.title: Embedded control has no accessible name
xlsx.description: An ActiveX or OLE control embedded in the workbook does not expose an accessible name or role in a form that static analysis can read. Assistive technology cannot identify or operate the control without it.

pdf.title: Image missing alt text
pdf.description: Every non-decorative Figure tag in the tag tree must have an /Alt entry. Screen readers read this entry when they encounter the figure.

pdf.title: PDF is not tagged
pdf.description: The document catalog must have MarkInfo.Marked=true and a complete structure (tag) tree. Without tags, screen readers have no semantic structure to navigate.

pdf.title: Document title not set
pdf.description: The document's /Info dictionary or XMP metadata must contain a non-empty /Title entry.

pdf.title: Document language not declared
pdf.description: The document catalog must include a /Lang entry with a BCP 47 language code. Screen readers use this to select the correct speech engine.

pdf.title: Reading order undefined
pdf.description: The logical order of tags in the structure tree must match the visual reading order on each page. Mismatched order causes screen readers to announce content out of sequence.

pdf.title: Viewer not set to show title
pdf.description: The viewer preferences dictionary must set /DisplayDocTitle to true so the window title bar shows the document title instead of the filename.

pdf.title: No navigation bookmarks
pdf.description: Multi-page documents should have an Outlines (bookmarks) tree so users can jump to sections without reading every page.

pdf.title: Instructions rely on sensory characteristics
pdf.description: Instructions that identify content solely by shape, visual position, size, or sound cannot be understood by users who are blind or deaf. Re-word to include a non-sensory alternative.

pdf.title: Insufficient colour contrast
pdf.description: Text fill colours in content streams must meet the 4.5:1 minimum contrast ratio against the resolved background for normal-sized text. The engine recolours failing text where the background can be structurally resolved.

pdf.title: Text baked into an image
pdf.description: An image appears to contain readable text. Text rendered into images cannot be resized, translated, or read by assistive technology. Extract the text into real PDF content.

pdf.title: Tab order not set to structure order
pdf.description: Pages containing AcroForm widgets must set /Tabs = /S in their page dictionary so the PDF viewer follows structure order when Tab is pressed. Without this, keyboard navigation order is undefined.

pdf.title: Link text is a raw URL
pdf.description: A hyperlink's visible text is the raw URL rather than a description of the destination. Screen reader users who navigate by links cannot determine the purpose of a raw URL link out of context.

pdf.title: Tagged PDF has no heading structure
pdf.description: A tagged PDF with no heading tags (H1–H6) provides no navigable structure. Screen reader users who jump by heading cannot skim the document. The engine proposes a heading map derived from font-size hierarchy for human confirmation.

pdf.title: Language of parts not marked
pdf.description: Passages of text in a language different from the document's /Lang must carry a /Lang attribute on their enclosing structure element. Without it, screen readers mispronounce foreign-language passages.

pdf.title: Form field has no accessible name
pdf.description: An AcroForm terminal field's /TU (tooltip / accessible name) entry is absent or generic. Screen readers announce /TU when focus reaches the field. The engine copies a meaningful /T value into /TU where available.
